questions.q: Cells A1:A5 contain: 72, Fail, 85, (blank), 90. What does =COUNTA(A1:A5) return?
questions.solution: COUNTA counts every non-empty cell - numbers and text alike: 72, 'Fail', 85, 90 = 4. The blank cell is the only one skipped.
questions.shortcut: COUNTA = Anything non-empty. COUNT would give 3 here.

questions.q: An antivirus program is best classified as:
questions.solution: Antivirus maintains and protects the system, which places it in utility software (along with defragmenters, backup tools, compressors).
questions.shortcut: 'Protect/maintain/clean' verbs -> utility. Antivirus is the most-asked utility example.

questions.q: The Windows feature that automatically detects and configures a newly connected USB printer is:
questions.solution: Plug and Play lets the OS identify new hardware, install its driver and configure it without manual setup. Hot swapping is only the connect/disconnect-while-running part; overclocking raises clock speed; mirroring is disk redundancy.
questions.shortcut: 'Automatically detects AND configures' = Plug and Play.

questions.q: In which topology is every node connected to every other node by a dedicated link?
questions.solution: Full mesh gives each pair of nodes its own direct link - maximum reliability at maximum cable cost (n(n-1)/2 links).

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

A group of lions
questions.solution: Lions live in a **pride**. *Herd* suits cattle, *swarm* bees, *flock* sheep or birds — the four collective options are swapped around in every paper.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (5).
questions.solution: The city pays residents to *take care of* the trees outside their homes: **look after**. *Look into* means investigate; *look down upon* means despise; *look up to* means admire. Only *look after* names an action whose absence would leave streets un-green and whose payment makes civic sense.
questions.shortcut: Substitute 'tend' — the option surviving the substitution wins.
questions.passage: Concrete has conquered our cities, and the first casualty has been the tree. A mature tree on a street does more than look (1) ______: it drops the temperature of its surroundings, traps dust and softens the noise of traffic. Yet when roads are widened, it is usually the tree that (2) ______ way. Municipal budgets treat planting as decoration rather than (3) ______, so saplings are planted in a rush before elections and forgotten soon afterwards. Survival, not planting, is the real (4) ______; a sapling needs watering for three full summers before it can stand on its own. Cities that have understood this simple point now pay residents a small sum to (5) ______ the trees outside their homes — and their streets are visibly greener.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The proteins in millets are higher than **most cereals**.
questions.solution: Proteins must be compared with proteins → **those of most cereals** (plural). 'That of' is singular; the original compares proteins with cereals — unlike things.
questions.shortcut: name both sides of the comparison before choosing.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

They are looking forward ___ their grandparents during the vacation.
questions.solution: In **look forward to**, 'to' is a preposition, so a gerund follows: **to meeting**. 'To meet' treats it as an infinitive — the classic trap. 'For meeting' uses the wrong particle, and bare 'meeting' drops the required to.

questions.q: The new series of the Consumer Price Index released in February 2026 uses which base year?
questions.solution: MoSPI's new CPI series (from 12 Feb 2026) shifts the base from **2012 to 2024**. 2022-23 is the new base for **GDP and IIP**, and the WPI moved to 2022-23 in June 2026.
questions.shortcut: Consumer prices anchor on a calendar year (2024); production series take financial years (2022-23).

questions.q: A light year is a unit of:
questions.solution: A **light year** is the **distance** light travels in one year — about **9.46 × 10¹⁵ m**. It is used for astronomical distances, not time.

questions.q: Laterite soil is mainly formed by which process?
options: Leaching under high temperature and heavy rainfall
questions.solution: **Laterite** forms where heavy rain and high heat **leach** away silica and lime, leaving iron and aluminium oxides. The name comes from Latin *later* (brick). River deposition gives alluvial soil, basalt weathering gives black soil and wind gives arid soils.

questions.q: The Sanskrit play **Mrichchhakatika** ('The Little Clay Cart') was written by —
questions.solution: **Shudraka** wrote *Mrichchhakatika*, a social drama about the Brahmin Charudatta and the courtesan Vasantasena. Bhasa – *Swapnavasavadatta*; Vishakhadatta – *Mudrarakshasa*; Dandin – *Dashakumaracharita*.

questions.q: What is the unit digit of $2^{51} + 3^{52} + 4^{53} + 5^{54}$?
Find the least number of five digits which is exactly divisible by 32, 36, 40, 45 and 48.
questions.solution:
LCM $= 2^5 \times 3^2 \times 5 = 1440$.
$10000 \div 1440$ gives remainder 1360, so $1440 - 1360 = 80$ more is needed.
Answer $= 10000 + 80 = 10080$.
questions.shortcut: LCM 1440; step 10000 up to the next multiple: 7 × 1440 = 10080.

questions.q: The compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years is:
The value of $\frac{1}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{6}}$ is:
questions.solution: Multiply top and bottom by $\sqrt7 + \sqrt6$: denominator $= 7 - 6 = 1$. Value $= \sqrt7 + \sqrt6$.

questions.q: **A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father.** How is **A related to D**?
questions.solution: A and B share the mother C; C is D's daughter. So D → C → A: two arrows up from A, and A is female → D's **granddaughter**. (Niece would need A to be a child of D's *sibling* — she is a child of D's child.)
questions.shortcut: Merge the sibling pair first; then it is one straight chain of two arrows.

questions.q: Select the related number: **? : 64 :: 5 : 125**
questions.solution: 5 : 125 is a **cube** pair (5³ = 125). So ? must satisfy ?³ = 64, and 4³ = 64. **Answer: 4.**
questions.shortcut: Blank first: read the rule from the full pair, then run it backwards (cube root here).

questions.q: Find the wrong term: **2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 38**
questions.shortcut: Differences 3, 5, 7, 9 are clean; the last gap (12) breaks the odd-number ladder.

questions.q: In which option is the figure given in the question **embedded** as a part (rotation is not allowed)?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 34 34" width="34" height="34" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="17" x2="17" y2="5"/><line x1="17" y1="5" x2="17" y2="17"/><line x1="17" y1="5" x2="29" y2="5"/><line x1="17" y1="17" x2="17" y2="29"/></svg>
questions.solution: The part is a / slant rising to a point, a horizontal line going right from that point and a vertical line going down from it. Only the first figure has the / slant cutting the top-left corner exactly where the vertical line meets the top edge; the top edge supplies the horizontal line. The second has the slant the other way; in the third no vertical line goes down from the upper end of the slant; in the fourth the slant is at the bottom.
questions.shortcut: Look for the part's most unusual stroke first; reject options where it is missing or runs the wrong way.
